name: Nival-Throne

civilization.name: Thraldom of the Pale Ascendancy
civilization.notes: A mountain-dwelling civilization that industrialized its way through the planet's dwindling geothermal warmth; their furnace-cities went cold within a single generation when the mantle convection stalled.

description: Nival-Throne is a world of impossible verticals: mountain ranges rising eleven kilometers above frozen methane plains, their flanks streaked with avalanche fans and hung with permanent frost-plumes. The thin atmosphere carries little weather, so the peaks stand eternally sharp, knife-edged against a bruise-purple sky. In the equatorial rift valleys, pools of liquid methane gather in terraces that descend like dark stairways into the ice.

The air is thin enough that sound barely travels, and what reaches the ear is mostly rock-tick and distant, muffled thunder from calving glaciers. Light has a metallic quality here, silver at noon and copper-red in the long dusk. Everything feels preserved—held—like a moment interrupted before it could finish.

The Pale Ascendancy built its furnace-cities into the warm hearts of these mountains, and their ruins still stand: tiered hab-shelves carved into cliff faces, heat-ducts wide enough to fly a shuttle through, and monoliths of black stone raised on every summit whose purpose no survey has explained. Their records suggest the civilization fell not to war or plague but to arithmetic—their mantle's convection stalled, geothermal taps cooled one by one, and an industrial society froze in place within forty years. The last messages etched near the summit monoliths translate, roughly, as 'we miscalculated.'

Salvage fleets covet Nival-Throne's titanium bones and the dark crystals embedded in the deep rifts, but the mountains have already claimed two mining concerns that pushed too fast into unstable ice-cliffs. Archaeologists warn that beneath the frozen cities lie sealed vaults the Ascendancy chose to close—and marked with warnings rather than maps. Whatever they locked away is still cold, still patient, and now slightly easier to reach.
